summary: The portfolio is built for a confirmed late-cycle regime: the Fed just delivered its first hike since 2023 to 3.75-4.00%, the real policy rate is +80-100bps above neutral, the 3m10y has re-inverted, PCE is running 175bps above target, and the equity risk premium is near zero vs a 5.01% 10-year yield — the most hostile valuation backdrop for long-duration growth in decades. The 10 growth picks express a selective, quality-momentum overlay: cybersecurity AI infrastructure (CRWD, PANW) as the highest-momentum group with fresh fundamental confirmation, enterprise AI software (CRM, META) where monetization is already in the P&L rather than 2-3 years out, energy value (MPC) capitalizing on the confirmed HALO trade at +57.3 vs SPY, healthcare quality (TMO, MRK) as late-cycle defensive rotation beneficiaries, and financial infrastructure compounders (SPGI, V) following Bill Ackman's Q2 conviction buys. Carry-overs from September 23: CRM (re-underwritten on FY2030 $63B target + director buy), META, MPC, TMO, MRK, SPGI — all re-qualified on fresh screen data and/or today's fundamental evidence. New additions: PANW (fresh platformization data — 220 net new Q4, NRR >120%), V (Ackman $1.12B Q2 initiator), NEM (gold proxy equity leverage). Removed: ZS (FY27 guidance deceleration to 16-17% growth + -38.4% off 52wk hi contradicts the momentum thesis), NET (dropped to add sector diversification — 4 IT names violated the 3-sector hard constraint), DE and ABBV (medium conviction replaced by higher-conviction challengers). The dominant risk being underwritten is an October FOMC hawkish surprise or hot September 30 PCE print compressing equity multiples from the current rich 22-23x — the defensive sleeve (GLD, SCHD, BRK.B, KO, NEE) is explicitly sized to absorb that scenario.

The defensive sleeve spans 4 distinct exposures: gold (GLD), broad dividend-quality equity (SCHD), diversified defensive conglomerate with cash optionality (BRK.B), consumer staples (KO), and utilities (NEE) — deliberately omitting long-duration Treasuries (TLT/IEF) given the Fed hiking cycle and 10Y at 5.01%.

### 1. 🔴 Regime Call: **Late-Cycle / Tightening Overshoot Risk**

The US economy is firmly in **late-cycle**, characterized by the paradox of strong nominal growth alongside a Fed actively re-hiking into above-trend output. 
Core PCE inflation expectations were revised up to 3.4% for 2026, requiring policy to stay restrictive longer, while GDP growth was revised upward to 2.3%, signaling that elevated rates have not yet triggered a slowdown.

1. **October 28 FOMC Decision + September CPI/PCE (due late September/October):** 
Ahead of the October meeting, the US will release August PCE, September payrolls, and September CPI; if core PCE, payrolls, and core CPI continue to show elevated inflation and robust employment, the market may increase probability of an October hike — cooling data, however, could shift expectations toward December.
